newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia approves draft deal on diamonds for Belarus.
newsitem.headline: Russia approves draft deal on diamonds for Belarus.

text.p: The Russian government has approved a draft agreement on supplying diamonds to Belarus in 1997, Interfax news agency said on Saturday.
Deputy Prime Minister Valery Serov has been ordered to make "changes and alterations to the draft of a non-fundamental nature" and sign the deal on the government's behalf, it said.
The draft involves supplying Belarus with up to 150,000 carats of gem diamonds and up to 350,000 carats of industrial diamonds in 1997.
Belarus will have to pay world prices for the diamonds and will not be allowed to re-export them, the agency said, citing from the draft document.
Under existing agreements with South Africa's De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd Russia is able to sell only a small percentage of its uncut diamonds independently.

Last October, shortly after a similar deal was signed for 1996, Itar-Tass news agency quoted the head of the De Beers Moscow office Raymond Clarke as saying the South African diamond giant had "no objections" to the Russian-Belarussian agreement.
